key_insight: Reference-free PINNs resolve strong kinetic normal shocks, with hard-sphere Boltzmann predictions differing from DSMC by at most 0.34% across eight evaluated fields at Mach 10.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a route to predicting strongly nonequilibrium shock structure and higher-order transport moments in high-speed gas flows.
method: Learn a signed, unbounded correction to an end-state Maxwellian mixture with exact inflow conditions.
Minimize kinetic residuals in three norms plus conservation terms, without reference data in the loss.
Combine Adam, self-scaled quasi-Newton optimization and Mach-number continuation.
evidence_signal: Post-training comparison with DSMC gives maximum relative L2 differences across eight fields of 0.19% at Mach 8 and 0.34% at Mach 10, with distribution-function agreement over six decades in velocity space.
watch_item: High-Mach BGK fourth-order moments require stronger weighting of a passive reduced distribution and longer optimization; errors remain up to 7.1% at Mach 100.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for strong normal shocks in kinetic relaxation models and the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
